summary.context: The requester describes a stuck bathtub overflow trip lever in an occupied San Francisco unit. More than five licensed plumbers were reportedly concerned that an above-access attempt could damage concealed plumbing. The storage space below may provide access through its ceiling. These details have not been independently inspected.
summary.recommendation: Start with Rapid Flow, Bay Area Plumbing / Save - On - Interior, Heise’s and Ace as inquiry leads. Rapid Flow has a relevant but unverified customer anecdote; Heise’s describes comparable tub waste-and-overflow work. None has confirmed this particular job.
summary.decision: Ask first for a non-destructive tub-side assessment. If that is not safe, request an itemized below-access alternative covering protection, opening, plumbing, testing, ceiling restoration and cleanup. Obtain written change-order terms before concealed work.
summary.limits: No provider was contacted. Quote attribution, price, exact capability, availability, tenant coordination, the assembly model and conditions behind the ceiling remain unverified.

providers.name: Rapid Flow Plumbing & Rooter Inc
providers.why: Company advertises plumbing and general contracting in San Francisco. A Yelp-indexed account for the same business name describes retrieving a stuck tub plug after opening a wall; the exact trip-lever fault and finish work are not established.
providers.review_note: One customer account, retrieved via search index; review and business match are not independently confirmed.
providers.caveat: Ask for a careful above-access assessment and one written plumbing-plus-ceiling-restoration scope.
providers.insurance_note: CSLB records a workers’ compensation exemption based on its no-employee certification.
providers.contact_note: CSLB lists (415) 866-8401; the company lists 844-229-3569 for calls and the CSLB number for texting photos.

providers.name: Bay Area Plumbing
providers.why: Company advertises San Francisco plumbing and shows a bathtub installation. CSLB personnel lists identify the same sole owner for this license and Save - On - Interior #749536 (B + C-36).
providers.caveat: Ask which licensed entity would contract, and whether it will include the complete ceiling finish. Similar name alone does not confirm the prior quote.
providers.insurance_note: CSLB records a workers’ compensation exemption based on its no-employee certification.

providers.name: Heise’s Plumbing
providers.why: Its own San Francisco job listing describes replacing tub waste-and-overflow assemblies; company also states it serves San Francisco.
providers.review_note: A BBB profile with the same phone and company website cites a different legal entity and license number; do not apply its history to this licensee without confirming the relationship.
providers.caveat: Ask if it can coordinate the ceiling restoration under one contract; exact stuck trip-lever extraction and timing are unconfirmed.

providers.name: Ace Plumbing & Rooter
providers.why: Company advertises residential plumbing and HOA/property-manager work in San Francisco; CSLB lists both B and C-36.
providers.review_note: BBB’s profile lists the same license number and displays customer comments about other plumbing jobs; BBB’s rating is not a review of this repair.
providers.caveat: Confirm an appropriately scoped single contract for plumbing, ceiling opening and finish, plus specific tub experience.

providers.name: Fast Response Plumbing & Rooter
providers.why: Company advertises residential plumbing, fixture work and service for San Francisco apartments and HOAs.
providers.review_note: A 2014 Angi customer account describes locating concealed bathroom access to clear a tenant’s drain; it is an older, different job and not independent proof of this scope.
providers.caveat: Confirm quote identity, exact work, finishing arrangements, and coverage; CSLB’s listed workers’ compensation policy expires 2026-12-18.

providers.name: Expert Plumbing Solutions
providers.why: Company advertises residential plumbing repairs, drains and fixture work in San Francisco. A Yelp-syndicated Yahoo Local excerpt reports an overflow leak repair, a different and not independently confirmed event.
providers.review_note: An August 2026 customer excerpt on Yahoo Local says the firm repaired a bathtub overflow leak; the excerpt is truncated and is not evidence of trip-lever extraction or drywall work.
providers.caveat: Confirm quote identity and whether the firm will coordinate access and drywall restoration.

providers.name: 24/7 SF Handyman & Remodeling Service

providers.caveat: B-2 has a three-unrelated-trade requirement and limits on system work; do not assume it covers this two-trade job. Verify classification and any specialty subcontractor.
providers.insurance_note: CSLB lists workers’ compensation coverage as of the check date.

technical.finding: Watco’s instructions for specific trip-lever models describe removing the overflow plate and drop-cylinder assembly for readjustment. This is a model-specific service path, not evidence that this installation can safely be extracted.
The same manufacturer instructions place the overflow elbow and gasket against the back of the tub. The installed assembly, condition and cause of sticking are not known.
Heise’s company listing describes San Francisco tub waste-and-overflow replacements. Whether this job needs the storage ceiling opened and who restores it must be determined on site.

CSLB’s B classification describes rules for prime contracts, including two unrelated trades and exceptions for appropriate specialty licensing or subcontracting. C-36 covers plumbing; confirm the actual contracting entity and scope.

technical.topic: B-2 is not interchangeable with B or C-36
technical.finding: CSLB’s classification description states that B-2 contracts are for existing residential wood-frame structures, require at least three unrelated trades and impose limits on plumbing-system work. Do not assume this specific job qualifies.

San Francisco DBI says a plumbing permit is needed before cutting into or replacing pipes, particularly pipes concealed by a wall, subject to listed exemptions. Confirm applicability and required inspection before covering work.
California Civil Code §1954 generally requires reasonable written notice for non-emergency entry; 24 hours is presumed reasonable absent contrary evidence. The statute includes exceptions.
The EPA describes lead-safe renovation rules for covered work in pre-1978 housing. The property’s age and material conditions have not been established.

CSLB recommends checking license status, insurance, references, a detailed written contract and cleanup. Confirm the ceiling’s required fire rating and any access-panel requirements before closure; these are site-specific.
